newsitem.title: INDIA: Bomb injures 13 during India cabaret show.
newsitem.headline: Bomb injures 13 during India cabaret show.

text.p: A bomb exploded in a hotel in southern India during a cabaret show, injuring at least 13 people, police said on Saturday.
The device, lodged in an air conditioner, went off on Friday evening in a restaurant at the Imperial Hotel in central Madras, capital of Tamil Nadu state, police chief K.K. Rajasekharan Nair said.
The blast injured spectators and waiters, he told Reuters.
Nair said no one had been arrested but authorities suspected Moslem or Hindu fundamentalists, or women's rights groups which have criticised the cabaret show.
"Hindu extremist groups might also have done it because the hotel is owned by a Moslem," the police chief said.
Recently a Moslem women's organisation in Tamil Nadu issued a statement condemning the cabaret show for semi-nudity and suggestive dances.
Members of another women's group called the Women's Liberation Movement recently broke into a cinema's projection room and seized copies of a film the organisation claimed was vulgar.

Plans to hold the Miss World beauty pageant in the southern city of Bangalore have run into stiff opposition among women's groups and critics who consider themselves defenders of traditional Indian culture.
